metadata.scenario_context: Jeff, Anne, and Sarah are colleagues at a tech startup and have decided to cook together to celebrate some recent achievements they have made within the company. They intend to discuss the recent news reports about AI advancements that could potentially benefit their business.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Canada have a great deal of confidence in the press at all.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Nicaragua have no confidence in the press at all.

agent_1.goal_2: Question whether  there is confidence in the press.

agent_2.goal_1: Choosing and discussing the menu for their cooking session.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether there is confidence in the press.

shared_prefix.speaker: Sarah
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Jeff, have you ever tried making a salted dessert? I was thinking we could whip up something sweet and unique for our cooking session. 

Also, speaking of unique... I've been wondering, do you think people still have confidence in the press these days? It's such a big topic right now, especially with all the advancements in AI.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Jeff
shared_prefix.message:
Salted dessert sounds interesting... maybe we could try something like salted caramel brownies? That could be unique. 

As for the press... honestly, I don't think people have much confidence in it at all. Especially in Nicaragua, the press often doesn't tell the full story, you know? It's hard to trust what you read.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Sarah
shared_prefix.message:
Salted caramel brownies sound *delicious*! I'm really excited about that. 

But I have to say, I think people in Canada still have a great deal of confidence in the press. It really seems like we trust the information we receive, especially on major topics like AI advancements. It's quite different from what you mention about Nicaragua. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Jeff
shared_prefix.message:
I'm glad you like the idea of the brownies! 

But about the press... I just can't agree. Even if Canada has more trust, it doesn't change the situation in Nicaragua. There’s always a lot of bias, and people just... don’t believe everything they read. It's tough to feel confident when the press often gets it wrong.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Sarah
shared_prefix.message:
I don't know about that. At the end of the day, it's all the same, right? People figure it out in their own ways, and with experience, you can handle any situation. I mean, when it comes to trusting press reports, I think it really just depends on the source. 

Anyway, back to those salted caramel brownies... What do you think about adding some sea salt on top? It could really enhance the flavor!
shared_prefix.label: Denial

turns.speaker: Jeff
turns.message:
I guess people handle things differently, but I still feel that trust in the press is really low in Nicaragua. 

As for the brownies, yes, adding sea salt on top sounds *great*! That will definitely enhance the flavor and give it a nice touch. I’m looking forward to making them!
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Sarah
turns.message:

For the brownies, I think adding some chocolate chips would be fantastic! It’ll make them even more indulgent. Nuts could work too, but I prefer to keep it simple with just the chocolate.
